# A Living Lexicon of Artificial Intelligence

> 91 concepts of artificial intelligence, one page each, in plain language. A book written with AI, which says so, and read critically by a peer.

A book by Stéphane Vial. Available October 13, 2026. Foreword by Marcello Vitali-Rosati. ISBN 978-2-9825534-2-2 (print) and 978-2-9825534-3-9 (ePUB). Translated from the French; translation revised by Alexia Moyer. © Stéphane Vial, publisher, 2026. Texts on this site are licensed under CC BY 4.0, unless otherwise noted. Pages that carry a “How to cite this text” section give the reference to use.

- Title: *A Living Lexicon of Artificial Intelligence*

**The author**

**Stéphane Vial**, Ph.D., is a Full Professor at the School of Design of the Université du Québec à Montréal, a regular researcher at the IUSMM Research Centre and the founder of Mentallys Inc. He holds a PhD in philosophy, a degree in clinical psychology and a habilitation to supervise research in design, and teaches, among other things, the use of artificial intelligence in research, writing and creative work.

The author of several books, including *Being and the Screen: How the Digital Changes Perception* (MIT Press), he explores how technologies transform our ways of perceiving, thinking and acting.

- About (in French): [stephane-vial.net](https://stephane-vial.net)
- Published books (in French): [stephane-vial.net/livres](https://stephane-vial.net/livres/)
- Blog on AI (in French): [stephane-vial.net/blog](https://stephane-vial.net/blog)
- Op-ed in *Le Devoir* (in French): [La mort de l’auteur n’aura pas lieu à l’ère de l’IA](https://www.ledevoir.com/opinion/idees/911919/mort-auteur-aura-pas-lieu-ere-ia)

**The 91 concepts, in eight chapters**

- **1. What Artificial Intelligence Is** (15 concepts): Imitation Game · Artificial Intelligence · Generative Artificial Intelligence · Algorithm · Model · Phases (of a Model) · Training · Inference · Fine-Tuning · Foundation Model · Agent · Alignment · Transparency · Explainability · Open Source
- **2. What an AI System Contains: Neurons and Parameters** (16 concepts): Perceptron · Neuron · Parameter · Weight · Bias (Parameter) · Activation Function · Layer · Neural Network · Backpropagation · Attention · Transformer · Language Model · Large Language Model · Reasoning Model · Diffusion Model · Multimodal
- **3. What (and How) AI Learns: Forms of Learning** (11 concepts): Learning · Machine Learning · Supervised Learning · Unsupervised Learning · Reinforcement Learning · Deep Learning · Dataset · Training Data · Personal Data · Pattern · Overfitting
- **4. What AI “Understands”: Language, Images, Sound** (9 concepts): Natural Language Processing · Chatbot · Generative Pre-trained Transformer · Machine Translation · Speech Recognition · Text-to-Speech · Computer Vision · Facial Recognition · Image Generator
- **5. The Language of Models: Tokens and Computation** (6 concepts): Token · Context Window · Vector · Probability · SoftMax · Temperature
- **6. What AI Produces: Answers, Errors, Hallucinations** (12 concepts): Input / Output · Prompt · Chain of Thought · Retrieval-Augmented Generation · Context Drift · Hallucination · Algorithmic Bias · Over-elaboration · Sycophancy · Black Box · Prompt Injection · Deepfake
- **7. AI in Our Digital Lives: Filters, Engines, Interfaces** (10 concepts): Personalization · News Feed · Recommender System · Collaborative Filtering · Ranking · Content Moderation · Spam Detection · Filter Bubble · Latency · Vibe Coding
- **8. Where Is Artificial Intelligence Going? Horizons, Risks, Questions** (12 concepts): Computing Power · Agentic AI · Artificial General Intelligence · Consciousness (Sentience) · AI Scheming · AI Psychosis · Existential Risk · AI Ecological Impact · AI Race · Sovereign AI · AI Governance · Responsible AI

## The book and its author

- [A Living Lexicon of Artificial Intelligence](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/): 91 concepts of artificial intelligence, one page each, in plain language. A book written with AI, which says so, and read critically by a peer.
- [91 concepts to understand artificial intelligence](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/book/): Ninety-one concepts, each explained in a page: a definition, an example, why it matters. No formulas, no code, no prerequisites. Eight entries to read.
- [The Making of This Book](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/making-of/): The account of how the book was made, as published in it: how a university professor wrote a book about AI with AI, and ran the whole publishing chain himself.
- [Statement on the Use of Artificial Intelligence](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/statement/): The statement published in the book: how artificial intelligence was used to write A Living Lexicon of Artificial Intelligence, and who answers for it.
- [A Montréal professor publishes a book about AI, written with AI](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/press-release/): Press release for the English edition of A Living Lexicon of Artificial Intelligence, by Stéphane Vial. Full text.
- [The author](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/author/): Stéphane Vial is a Full Professor at the School of Design of UQAM. He holds a PhD in philosophy, a degree in clinical psychology and a habilitation to supervise research in design.
- [Order the book](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/order/): Where to buy A Living Lexicon of Artificial Intelligence, by Stéphane Vial: on Amazon, in paperback and Kindle editions. Press contact.

## Eight entries to read, one per chapter

- [Artificial Intelligence](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/book/artificial-intelligence/): Chapter 1 · page 22. Artificial intelligence (AI) refers to a set of computational methods and systems able to reproduce or simulate certain capacities usually associated with human intelligence.
- [Neuron](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/book/neuron/): Chapter 2 · page 40. An artificial neuron is a computing unit whose name and general principle are borrowed, in simplified form, from biological neurons.
- [Machine Learning](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/book/machine-learning/): Chapter 3 · page 58. Machine learning is a branch of artificial intelligence that lets a system learn from data rather than being programmed rule by rule.
- [Natural Language Processing](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/book/natural-language-processing/): Chapter 4 · page 71. Natural language processing refers to a set of computational methods that allow a machine to process, interpret and produce human language, written or spoken.
- [Token](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/book/token/): Chapter 5 · page 83. In artificial intelligence, a token is the smallest unit of text that language models handle.
- [Hallucination](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/book/hallucination/): Chapter 6 · page 96. A hallucination is the phenomenon by which a model generates false, invented, distorted or misleading information while presenting it with apparent coherence or confidence.
- [Recommender System](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/book/recommender-system/): Chapter 7 · page 107. A recommender system is an algorithmic system designed to automatically offer content, products or services to a user based on their preferences, their past behaviour or that of users judged to be similar.
- [Agentic AI](https://web.stephane-vial.net/lexique-ia/en/book/agentic-ai/): Chapter 8 · page 118. Agentic AI refers to artificial intelligence systems capable of acting semi-autonomously or autonomously to reach a goal, often over several steps.
